question: ATK Lotus 5v5, your team is fixing DEF attention on B, you lurk A Tree near the rotating A door. How do you exploit the door mechanic for your lurk?

options.label: Trigger the A rotating door to fake a push toward A and bait a DEF to check, then punish from your lurk position
options.explication_courte: On Lotus the door audio cue is a fake tool: triggering the door sounds like an A take and draws a DEF to check, whom you punish from lurk while your team fixes B.

options.label: Cross the A door to actually take A space and threaten a real A/B split
options.explication_courte: Taking real A space creates a genuine double-threat, but crossing the door reveals your lurk position and exposes you alone to an A anchor without your team trading.

sources_option.citation: Actually taking A space through the door creates a real split threat but sacrifices the lurker's surprise and exposes them to the A anchor without team trade.

options.label: Place your Trademark in the door opening to cover your flank during the lurk
options.explication_courte: Placing Trademark inside the door rotation radius causes it to be destroyed when the door turns - you lose your flank coverage tool, exactly the Lotus mechanic trap.

sources_option.citation: Anything sitting in a rotating door's path gets destroyed the instant it spins; deployables like Chamber's Trademark are lost if placed in the rotation arc.

options.label: Trigger the door every round to always fake A as a recurring pattern
options.explication_courte: Faking the door every round makes the fake predictable: DEF stop respecting it and your lurk loses all value. The fake only works used sparingly.

sources_option.citation: You can trigger door sounds to fake a rotation, but make sure you don't use this trick too frequently — a predictable fake stops distracting defenders.

explication_longue:
Situation: ATK Lotus 5v5, your team is fixing DEF attention on B, you lurk A Tree near the rotating A door. The question: how do you exploit the door for your lurk?

Lurk principle: create value when the team fixes attention elsewhere. On Lotus, the rotating A door has a unique property: its sound when triggered (a loud mechanical rotation) mimics the sound of a player taking A space. This makes it a free information tool and a fake vector - triggering the door from outside causes DEF monitoring A to react (a rotating DEF = a punishable moment, or a DEF who stays = confirmed A anchor intel).

Optimal sequence: trigger the door without crossing, observe if a DEF rushes to A to check, and punish the rotation from your lurk position. Crossing the door for real A space (acceptable) creates a genuine double-threat but gives away your lurk. Placing Trademark in the rotation radius (costly) is the classic Lotus mechanic trap - the door destroys it. Triggering the door every round (mistake) trains DEF to ignore it.

Estimated elite distribution: ~54% trigger as fake then punish rotation, ~22% cross door for real A space, ~16% Trademark in rotation radius (costly), ~6% trigger every round (mistake).

sources.citation: Use the rotating doors to fake one site and hit another; you can trigger these sounds to make enemies think you plan to rotate, causing distraction — but don't use it too frequently.
The rotating door audio cue can bait defenders into checking an angle; a lurker near the door can punish the reaction while the team pressures another site.
Never park deployable utility in a door's rotation path; anything in the arc is destroyed the instant it spins, so lurkers must place trademarks clear of the door.
